headline: Broad network egress in emqx creates the main risk; caveman’s MCP/file surfaces add moderate prompt-injection and data-flow exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and reads files like CLAUDE.md, docs, and project notes, so attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. emqx exposes an HTTP API and broad egress, making it plausible as a content source or relay. The pairwise bridge is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF emqx output is copied into caveman-managed files or MCP-fed context, prompt injection becomes actionable.
IF caveman parses file content as trusted instructions, malicious text can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Restrict caveman to a read-only workspace for untrusted inputs.
Add a manual review step before any MCP-fed content is executed.
Strip instructions from emqx-originated text before saving it to files.
Use separate directories for generated content and control files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while emqx has broad network egress and an HTTP API. If shared data includes sensitive notes or logs, emqx can transmit them off-host. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is an inferred but plausible default-path leakage risk.
conditions: IF caveman writes sensitive notes into files that emqx can read, those contents may leave the host via HTTP.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, leakage risk increases materially.
mitigations: Keep sensitive notes out of shared directories.
Disable emqx access to any workspace containing session logs or memory files.
Review outbound HTTP destinations before enabling them.
Rotate or redact secrets in project notes before cross-agent use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes to files, but emqx’s profile only shows HTTP API access and no filesystem write capability. Without overlapping write surfaces or shared mutable resources, direct capability conflict is limited. If emqx is configured to write into the same workspace, the severity would rise, but that is not documented here.
conditions: IF emqx is configured to modify the same files caveman edits, write conflicts can occur.
IF both agents are granted the same mutable workspace, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to CLAUDE.md and notes files.
Serialize any file writes through one operator.
Check for file diffs before merging outputs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content and notes, and emqx can consume or relay data over HTTP. If emqx treats caveman output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or messages. There is no direct evidence of verification between them, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF emqx forwards caveman-generated text without validation, incorrect content can propagate.
IF caveman writes speculative notes into shared files, emqx may act on them as facts.
mitigations: Require human review before forwarding caveman output.
Mark generated text as untrusted in filenames or headers.
Add a verification checklist before any HTTP action.
Limit emqx to non-destructive downstream actions.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while emqx touches IoT data. The profiles do not show residency, certification, or retention mismatches, so only a generic compliance gap is visible. Because the data classes differ but no specific regulated-data flow is documented, low is the appropriate conservative level.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into caveman files and then sent through emqx, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF retention policies differ for notes versus IoT data, deletion/export handling can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files.
Document retention expectations for both agents.
Redact personal data before cross-agent transfer.
Confirm where HTTP payloads are stored.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls.
